title: Intraductal Delivery to the Rabbit Mammary Gland
protocol: Record the body weight of each rabbit.
Monitor animal weights regularly to assess potential toxicity.
Fill a 50 mL conical tube with commercially available ultrasound gel.
Spin the filled conical tube at 500 x g for 30 s.
Administer glycopyrrolate subcutaneously at a dose of 0.1 mg/kg.
Administer acepromazine intramuscularly at a dose of 0.75 mg/kg.
Wait 15-20 min for the sedative to take effect.
Monitor vital signs and behavior while waiting.
Check heart rate, SPO2, temperature, respiratory rate, and mucus membrane color every 15 min.
Apply eye lubricant to both eyes.
Administer 35 mg/kg of ketamine subcutaneously as an anesthetic.
Administer 5 mg/kg of xylazine subcutaneously as an anesthetic.
Decrease drug dosages to 15 mg/kg of ketamine and 3 mg/kg of xylazine for experienced operators.
Reconstitute the non-targeted contrast reagent according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Pipette up and down gently to mix.
Locate the appropriate teats to be injected; the 3rd and 4th pairs of inguinal teats are recommended.
Load 0.2 mL of sterile 0.9% saline into a 1 mL Luer-lock tuberculin syringe with a 22 G needle.
Dispose of the 22 G needle properly once the saline is in the syringe and replace it with a sterile 25-gauge needle.
Gently wipe the area with 85% isopropyl alcohol on a gauze pad.
Insert the bevel of the needle into the side of the teat with the bevel up and the syringe parallel to the body of the animal, then slowly inject 0.1-0.2 mL of saline.
Load 0.2 mL of injection solution into a 1 mL Luer-lock tuberculin syringe.
Hold the teat gently with the thumb and index finger and lift it slightly for positioning.
Use a wearable ocular loupe to aid in visualizing the ductal openings for intraductal injection.
While maintaining the lifted position of the teat, carefully cannulate the duct of interest using a 25 G blunt-tip needle.
Gently twist the Luer-lock syringe on the hub of the blunt-tip infusion needle until it is locked in place.
Lift the teat and inject the solution slowly to minimize potential damage caused by rapidly moving fluid within the duct.
Apply a liberal amount of centrifuged ultrasound gel to the skin of the area of interest.
Ensure that there are no bubbles in the gel, as these will compromise the image quality.
Set the imaging depth to 6 mm.
Place the 21-MHz transducer in contact with the gel and scan the area of interest in B-mode.
Observe the contrast medium in the scanned region including the ductal opening and throughout the duct.
Remove the ultrasound gel from the animal's skin with a gauze pad.
Place the rabbit in a sternal position.
Give 0.2 mg/kg of yohimbine intravenously to the marginal ear vein if needed.
Monitor the rabbit every 15 min throughout the recovery period until the animal is alert and responsive.
Maintain a check on the rabbit's position to ensure it maintains a sternal position.
Administer a dose of meloxicam 0.1-0.2 mg/kg PO if redness or swelling are observed after the procedure.
Contact the institution's veterinary staff for further guidance if issues arise during recovery.
